title: Unlimited Health Insurance: What to Check Before You Buy
description: The term "unlimited health insurance" often refers to high sum insured plans, not truly limitless coverage. Policy exclusions define specific conditions or tr.

faq.q: What are pre-existing diseases (PEDs) in health insurance?
faq.a: Pre-existing diseases are any medical conditions, illnesses, or injuries that an insured person had within 48 months prior to purchasing the health insurance policy. These are typically covered after a specific waiting period, usually 2-4 years, as defined by IRDAI regulations.

faq.q: Can I get cashless treatment with an "unlimited" policy?
faq.a: Yes, a high sum insured policy usually offers cashless treatment, provided the hospital is part of the insurer's network. The cashless facility is still subject to all policy terms, conditions, deductibles, co-payments, and sub-limits.

faq.q: Are maternity benefits always included in health insurance?
faq.a: No, maternity benefits are often an add-on or included in specific plans with a significant waiting period, typically ranging from 9 months to 4 years. It's crucial to check if your policy explicitly covers maternity and its associated waiting period.

faq.q: How do deductibles affect my premium?
faq.a: Generally, opting for a higher deductible in your health insurance policy can lead to a lower premium. This is because you are agreeing to bear a larger portion of the initial claim amount, thereby reducing the insurer's risk.

faq.q: Can I port my health insurance policy to another insurer?
faq.a: Yes, IRDAI regulations allow you to port your health insurance policy from one insurer to another, retaining the continuity benefits, especially for waiting periods for pre-existing diseases. You need to apply for portability at least 45 days before your policy renewal date.

faq.q: Is the premium for health insurance tax-deductible?
faq.a: Yes, premiums paid for health insurance policies are eligible for deduction under Section 80D of the Income Tax Act, 1961. The deduction limits vary based on age and whether the policy covers senior citizens.
